verifier_note: Checked against: the pinned rapier3d-f64 0.35.3 source on disk (cross-referenced live against docs.rs), the rapier.rs Rust-0.36 guide, the raw dimforge/rapier CHANGELOG.md fetched directly at both the v0.35.3 and v0.36.0 tags (not the summarized WebFetch version, which mis-split two 0.35.0 vs 0.35.0-beta.0 entries on a first pass), crates.io's versions API, GitHub issue #1008, two Cargo-book pages, and the si-rpg-engine repo at main (rapier_law.rs, FLAGS.md, Cargo.toml/.lock, rust-toolchain.toml, ci.yml, and the T1-T4/rust-kb-requests dispatch docs). I ran every one of the lane's 23 checks through the real pinned compiler via compile_oracle.py and independently hand-wrote and ran the two mandated high-stakes counter-examples (thin-slab CCD, wake_up-vs-iter_mut re-admission) myself: all 23 checks passed, and my two reproductions matched the recipe's predicted stdout byte-for-byte, including deliberately surprising results (a 0.35.3 doc comment stale at 0.002m/0.001x while its own Default impl already reads 0.02/0.005; PhysicsWorld::wake_up failing to re-admit a body that plain iter_mut() fixes; a debug_assert literally on island_manager/manager.rs line 140; commit 39687d9's message matching the recipe's E3 account word for word). What failed: two of ten recipes cite si-rpg-engine dispatch docs (T4 pin 2 in the IntegrationParameters-defaults lane, T3 pin 6 in the collision-events lane) as still holding an open question or a wrong assumption that the live document on main has already closed or corrected; both are marked corrected rather than refuted, since every Rust/crate claim in those two recipes is independently solid. Recipe 1's step-order prose also over-compresses one detail (joint 'joins' drain after quarantine/user-changes, not alongside wake-ups as written). The one systemic weakness: this lane's Rust/rapier sourcing is exceptionally disciplined -- of roughly 40 external sources and 20-odd direct source-file claims I checked, none were wrong -- but its engine_notes are perishable, because they cross-reference the coordinating T-dispatch docs' state as of authoring time and this repo amends those same-day (T4 pin 2 carries an explicit 'Amended 2026-09-25' note); an engine_note is only as fresh as its last re-check against main, and this sweep found it had already drifted out from under two of the ten recipes.
